ConocoPhillips rose slightly today, but remains down sharply over the past two weeks as oil prices have weakened on geopolitical developments. On Monday, President Trump signaled that the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon," which eased concerns about Middle East supply disruptions—Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August. With global oil prices now at $107, down from the tension premium that had pushed them higher, upstream producers like ConocoPhillips face lower revenue per barrel, even though U.S. crude is holding relatively steady at $99.64.

The stock's 8% drop over two weeks reflects the market repricing oil demand and geopolitical risk downward. When investors believe a major supply threat is diminishing, they're willing to pay less for barrels—a direct headwind for companies whose profits depend on what they can sell oil for.
